public_title: Efficacy and Safety of Medical Cannabis in Parkinson's disease
hc_freetext: Parkinson disease patients are suffered from motor and non-motor symptoms.
i_freetext: The cannabis oil (CBD:THC 1:1) were titrate with dose escalation schedule until achieved the satisfied effect for releasing Parkinson's symptoms. The maximum duration was 6 weeks. The evaluation of the response of treatment was done every 2 weeks.,The placebo was rice bran oil which had indistinguisable character by color and texture. The dose titration schedule, duration and evaluation method were similar as the active comparator arm.
prim_outcome: Global score of parkinson symptoms Every 2 weeks until 6 weeks after end of intervention MDS-UPDRS
sec_outcome: Motor score of Parkinson disease Every 2 weeks until 6 weeksafter end of the intervention MDS-UPDRS part III,Motor complication score of Parkinson disesase Every 2 weeks until 6 weeks after end of the intervention MDS-UPDRS part IV,safety of the product use Every 2 weeks until 6 weeks after the intervention Interview
results_summary: Thirteen patients (86.7%) completed the entire trial. There were no statistically significant changes in the total MDS-UPDRS. The mean chnages score were 47.3 and 49.3 in the cannabis group and placebo group respectively (p 0.461). There was no major adverse effect reported although there were 2 dropouts in the cannabis group related to the intolerability of the side effects. One elderly patient had acute kidney injury that may be related to cannabis use.
